added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs: logs/after-arm-failing-files-base.log (revision cb1b92d1ce) and logs/importers-subset-after.log (revision 6013d3c3b6) each end "21 failed, 331 passed" with EXIT=1 and list the same 21 FAILED ids, so zero ids appear at the head that the base did not carry; the shared causes are pre-existing (role 'implement' is not configured, TaskNode.__init__ missing 'plan', KeyError 'argv').

findings.text: assert receipt["reason"] == "the record stopped before it measured anything" compares the string the test passed in through --reason against the receipt's echo of it, so it holds for any code that echoes its argument and cannot redden on a repair that changed nothing.

the module docstring records the prior behaviour ("the repair verb knew only ... had no repair path at all") rather than the invariant the tests assert, which is changelog prose in a source docstring and rots once the defect is historical.

the project reaches the repair only through _accept_a_matching_project, whose fallback is the --project argument, so a committed record whose run has neither a live pointer nor a ledger record is still refused as outside the review-records directory unless the operator adds --project, which is the same refusal §26 exists to remove.

item_verdicts.done_when: §26's done-when names two cases, the importer arm, ruff and a declared negative control; the manifest records the node gate 2 passed EXIT=0 in logs/node-gate.log and the control 1 failed 1 passed EXIT=1 in logs/negative-control-staging-only-directory-check.log, and the two importer arms carry identical 21-id failure sets.

item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, ten log paths named, baseline_suite at cb1b92d1ce completed with 21 failures and after_suite at 6013d3c3b6 completed with the same 21, and the declared negative control log named.
